Rules / Modernization

SK1011 Use a property pattern

A stable reference's null guard followed by one member equality can be expressed as a property pattern.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 8.0
Since1.3

Why

A property pattern combines the receiver's non-null requirement and a member condition. Restricting this rewrite to one member retains getter evaluation count and avoids reordering getters. Stable, non-ref, uncaptured locals and parameters avoid replacing two observable receiver reads with one.

Example

Instead of:

bool IsReady(Item item) => item != null && item.Ready == true;

Write:

bool IsReady(Item item) => item is { Ready: true };

When it does not fire

Only a non-null guard (is not null or built-in != null) and one == constant comparison are supported. The receiver must be stable local or parameter storage with no capture or ref escape. Supported member constants are integral, char, bool, enum, string and eligible null comparisons. Float, decimal, overloaded equality, conversions with different semantics, expression trees, directives and interior comments are excluded. Chained getters and multiple member tests are not consolidated.
